### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-component-types.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-print-page-blocks.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-component-types.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-print-page-blocks.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c7a44fe9ce8cb2dab65098a6c186e1ece6dd9459` — the merge of head `3301d5f2f1545c2bcc0e566254c0b0597ab85941` into base `394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c7a44fe9ce8cb2dab65098a6c186e1ece6dd9459 && git checkout c7a44fe9ce8cb2dab65098a6c186e1ece6dd9459
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520 3301d5f2f1545c2bcc0e566254c0b0597ab85941 && git checkout -B drift-repro 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520 && git merge --no-ff 3301d5f2f1545c2bcc0e566254c0b0597ab85941

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ba20e780ec9f344104d6a17c19f47f38b68a74ab`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23388 (body + 5 comments: delta 6160833647, ruling of record 6161173492 letter B, triage 6161267305, claim 6161640267, os-dev report 6163297010); PR #23418 body, 35-file list, net diff `main...ba20e780e` (merge base `e4ec6ec1a`, 2 commits, +289/−136); the 39 check-runs on the head, read once.

**Check-runs on the head (their conclusions are the gate verdicts).** Success: Auto Label · Check Documentation Links · Check PR Size · Dogfood Regression Gate · Flag docs affected by code changes · Governed Surface Queue Guard · Lint · CI, release & engine gates · Lint · PM dispatch-gates · Lint · scoped · query-options erasure · Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus · Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests · No other open PR may claim the same issue · No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path · Part-of PR must not also close its card · Spec property liveness · The card this PR closes must claim this branch · Type Check · source gates · filter. **Failure: Check Changeset** — the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class (`pr-automation.yml` route 0, ruling D on #18375): the PR rewrites two pending changesets it did not add; that job is not a required context and is red by design, judged in ③-1 below. Skipped (not applicable): Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance. **In progress at brief time** (named, not watched): Build Core · Lint · ESLint · Lint · docs & code guards · Lint · repo & tooling gates · Test Core (1/6)–(6/6) · Type Check · consumer gates · Type Check · debt ledger · Type Check · workspace. The four gates the dev reported NOT MEASURED locally (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:query-options-erasure`) are answered by those CI jobs; `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure` is already green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`validateComponentProps`: `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` → `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['page']`** (`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`). An accept-set narrowing on the metadata save door for `page` writes: `saveMetaItem` active save, `publishMetaItem` draft→active promotion, REST `PUT /api/v1/meta/page/:name`, MCP through `runtime-authoring-gate.ts`. A page whose component carries an undeclared, wrong-typed or retired property is refused `422 INVALID_METADATA` with the rule's existing finding (`component-props-unknown-key` / `component-props-invalid`), fix included. **Right** — ruling item 1, verbatim. `page` already maps to `pages` in `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY` (`runtime-gate.ts:99`), so no mechanism edit was owed and none was made.
2. **`validateComponentTypes`: same crossing, same PR.** A component `type` inside a spec-reserved namespace the platform does not declare is refused (`component-type-unknown`) with the rename; a type outside the reserved namespaces (`acme:pipeline_board`) still saves. **Right** — ruling item 2; the open string arm is untouched (pinned by the control).
3. **Both `surfaceReason`s removed, `runtimeTypes` added.** The wiring guard (`authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts`) requires exactly this pair for a runtime-published rule and refuses a reason shorter than 40 chars on a CLI-only one; the diff leaves neither half-written. **Right.**
4. **Read and boot path unchanged.** `loadMetaFromDb` / `getMetaItem` run no authoring rule; a stored page carrying both findings loads (`loaded: 1, errors: 0, invalid: 0`), registers and is served as stored; its next save is refused and the row is untouched; the fixed page saves. **Right** — ruling item 4(b) and the precedent sentence at `18.page-default-record-page-one-per-object-refused.ts:42`. A draft save is not judged until promotion, consistent with the gate's existing draft semantics, and the promotion is pinned as no bypass.
5. **Rule text, `ComponentPropsMap`, `validate-component-props.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `page.zod.ts`, `component.zod.ts` untouched.** The card's protocol line and the claim's ⛔ list are honoured; the file list carries none of #23357's or #23332's files.
6. **#4716 citations rewritten to cite ruling 6161173492** in both entry comments, both `surfaceReason`s (deleted), the `validatePrintPageBlocks` entry comment, and the two sibling rule headers (`validate-component-types.ts`, `validate-print-page-blocks.ts`). **Right** — ruling item 3. The header block at ~494–511 (`RUNTIME_OBJECT_ADVISORY_VOLUME`) describes the #4716 split of the OBJECT rules and names neither page rule; leaving it is right.
7. **Door asymmetry on two live-window aliases — a real accept-set consequence, correctly disclosed.** The runtime gate hands every rule the body as written (`runtime-gate.ts` `runRules` → `rule.run(stack, ctx)`); the CLI feeds a rule declared `input: 'normalized'` the D2-converted stack (`authoring-rules.ts:2242`). So `page:header` `description` and an inline `type: 'api'` action's object `params` (conversions `page-header-subtitle-alias`, `inline-action-api-params-to-body-extra`, `toMajor: 17`, not yet `retiredFromLoadPath`) are converted by `os validate` but refused at the save door, with the canonical key named. The changeset's "Who is affected" paragraph says so, and stored rows are rehydrated through the conversions on read. **Named right as a disclosed narrowing beyond the ruling's three classes**, carried as flag ③-6 (a follow-up, not a blocker: the refusal carries the fix, the maintainer's principle is fix-then-save, and the asymmetry is the gate's pre-existing raw-body behaviour, shared with `validatePrintPageBlocks`).
8. **Two pending changesets corrected** (`23147-…`: the sentence "the runtime publish door … does not run this rule" deleted; `23103-…`: "a stored page still saves and loads" → loads, next save refused by the same gate). Both sentences are made false by judgment 1; the corrections say only what the diff makes true. **Right** (process in ③-1).
9. **24 step-18 D3 entries + `registry.ts.template`: text only.** Each `reason` / rationale string that said "a stored page still saves and loads" now says it still loads and its next save meets the component-props gate at the save door; code comments "never refused" → "never refused at load". These strings are shipped in `os migrate meta` and the upgrade guide, so correcting them in the same change is right; no key, schema, conversion or entry id moves; `registry.ts` is gitignored and regenerated. **Right, with two nits** (③-2): in the `ui-object-grid-export-options-closed` and `ui-object-master-detail-form-details-closed` rationale fragments the concatenation `'…still loads '` + `' and no conversion…'` yields a double space in the rendered text; five D3 code comments keep "not parsed on the metadata save or load path, so a stored page is never refused at load" (comment-only, slightly self-contradictory; the `reason` strings beside them are correct).
10. **Pins (ruling item 4)** in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`, through the real `saveMetaItem` / `publishMetaItem` / `loadMetaFromDb` / `getMetaItem`: (a) undeclared prop refused with `` `titel` → `title` `` and `Remove `titel``, nothing stored, `rulesRun` names both rules, draft promotion refused too; (c) `page:headr` refused with hint exactly `` Rename `page:headr` → `page:header`. ``; control saves the declared spelling and the out-of-namespace type; (b) as in judgment 4. All helpers used (`makeProtocol`, `makeStubEngine`, `keyOf`, `Row`, `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`) exist in the file. **Right**; the dev's ablation legs (props rule back to `CLI_ONLY` reds (a)+(b); types rule back reds (c)+(b)+(a)) show each pin reads its rule.
11. **No public API, export, type or schema moves**: no `index.ts`, no `*.zod.ts`, no `protocol.ts`; `@objectstack/lint`'s only public-surface change is the registry's behaviour on the runtime door. No governed path (Governed Surface Queue Guard green). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23388-page-component-rules-runtime-door.md`: `'@objectstack/lint': minor` with the **BREAKING** banner, `'@objectstack/spec': patch`. **Matches the diff.** The narrowing lives in `@objectstack/lint`'s registry; under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, maintainer ruling 2026-09-04) a breaking change ships as `minor` and breaking-ness is carried by the banner and the ADR-0087 disposition — both present (`not-required (already-registered …)`, listing the same D3 ids the 23147 note names; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` is green). `major` would also have passed under the RC exemption (`pre.json` mode `pre`), as 23147 chose; `minor` is the convention and is right. `@objectstack/spec` moves only `reason` text in migration entries and the registry template, so `patch` is right. The changeset carries the ruling's item-5 sentence verbatim ("The next save of a stored page … is refused with the fix; stored pages keep serving until then."), names the doors, the FROM → TO table, the measured-population caveat and the alias asymmetry. Not `skip-changeset`, correctly — the `skip-changeset` label is refused on a PR that edits an existing changeset (ruling D, #18375) and none was applied.

Clause-②: no — an accept-set narrowing on a published door; the PR body, the changeset, the claim and triage all say `no`, and this review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the review the narrowing owes before the queue.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev flag — deliberate correction of two pending changesets; `check:empty-changeset` / Check Changeset red by design.** *Answered: accepted.* Route 0 of the workflow fits exactly: both rows are `M`, the before-sentences are made false by this diff's `surfaces` line, the rewritten text says nothing the diff does not make true, the PR body carries the written confirmation naming each note and the change under it, no `skip-changeset` label was applied, and the job is not a required context. ~~This record, once adopted, is the confirmation "in writing" the route asks for;~~ *(struck by the adopting seat: route 0 in `pr-automation.yml` puts the decision "in front of a person" and "the approver merges over it", so the confirmation is the maintainer's, not this record's; it is requested on this PR.)* The red stands.
2. **Dev flag — file surface beyond the claim** (`validate-print-page-blocks.ts`, `validate-component-types.ts` headers; 24 D3 entries; `registry.ts.template`; the two changesets), on os-dev's "shipped text a change makes false is fixed in that change" overriding the claim's "stop on a breach". *Answered: accepted.* Every edit is text that judgment 1 falsifies, none touches a file #23357 or #23332 holds, none is a governed path, and `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide` are reported green with the `Lint · docs & code guards` job still in progress. The two nits in judgment 9 (double space in two rationale fragments; five code comments still reading "save or load path … never refused at load") are cosmetic and comment-level; fix in passing on the next touch of those files, no new card.
3. **Dev flag — ruling item 3 "header lines that name them" (~494–511).** *Answered: verified.* Those lines are `RUNTIME_OBJECT_ADVISORY_VOLUME`, about the #4716 OBJECT-rule split; they do not name either page rule and remain true. No other header in the file names the two rules with the old budget after this diff.
4. **Dev out-of-scope finding — `packages/lint/src/validate-component-props.ts:111–116`** ("The runtime publish door … does not run this rule … a page saved there is not refused") becomes false on landing; file held by #23357 (seat 1). *Escalated:* the owning seat relays it to #23357's PR (that PR already owes the deletion of the narrow judge under ruling item 6); if #23357 lands without it, a one-line follow-up on this card's thread.
5. **Dev out-of-scope finding — `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:5991–5994`** doc comment ("a stored page still saves and loads"); file held by #23332 (this seat). *Escalated:* fold into #23332's PR as a comment-only line; no card.
6. **Dev out-of-scope finding, class b — the save door refuses two live-window page aliases that `os validate` converts** (`page:header` `description` → `subtitle`; inline api action `params` → `bodyExtra`; both `toMajor: 17`, `retiresIn` 18, neither `retiredFromLoadPath`). *Escalated — a follow-up card, filed by the owning seat with the dev's dedupe words (`retiredFromLoadPath step 18`, `page-header-subtitle-alias`, `inline-action-api-params-to-body-extra`, `live-window conversion overdue`).* Two routes for that card: retire the two overdue aliases from the load path at 18 (then the CLI and the door agree by construction), or have the runtime gate feed `input: 'normalized'` rules a D2-converted body (a gate-wide change that also touches `validatePrintPageBlocks`). Not a blocker here: the refusal names the canonical key, the maintainer's principle is fix-then-save, and the changeset discloses it.
7. **`open_questions`: []** — none to answer.
8. **Ruling item 6 (the #23357 narrow judge is deleted once this lands)** is not this PR's work and is correctly left to #23357's PR or a one-line follow-up; the PR body says so for the seat.
